title: feat(status-pages): default layout with status banner, paged history and incident calendar

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge 1 warning −1 · 1/2 new units observable −1 Reworks the public status page layout and adds a 12-month incident history with a calendar, nonce-safe JSON data for the client-side tooltips and pagers, and privacy/terms footer links carried through DB, v2 API and editor. Escaping, window math and schema changes are pinned by tests; one unbounded year-long incident read needs a cap. - `renderPage` gains hero banner, paged 90-day uptime bars, incident calendar and footer links - Snapshot gains `incidentHistory` (`STATUS_PAGE_HISTORY_DAYS` 90 → 365) and `page.privacyUrl`/`termsUrl` - `STATUS_PAGE_CONFIG_VERSION` check rejects configs with invalid footer URLs - `sp-data` JSON script replaces per-bar inline handlers; `script.ts` reads and paginates it ### Before merge - [ ] **Migration** · Check it is safe on production data and with the code still deployed · [`packages/db/drizzle/20261029152817_status_page_footer_links/migration.sql`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/f58bd75da833e9094811f126f59dc6a6fbcc5eee/packages/db/drizzle/20261029152817_status_page_footer_links/migration.sql) - [ ] **Manual** · Apply `20261029152817_status_page_footer_links` in the prd alchemy deploy (adds nullable `privacy_url`/`terms_url`) ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F1 · Year-long incidents read has no limit, so the public page payload grows unbounded performance · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts:366`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/f58bd75da833e9094811f126f59dc6a6fbcc5eee/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts#L366) The cutoff moved from `STATUS_PAGE_INCIDENT_HISTORY_DAYS` (14) to `STATUS_PAGE_HISTORY_DAYS` (365) and the query still has no `limit` or `orderBy`, so every incident resolved in the last year (plus every unresolved one) is read and, through `incidentHistory`, embedded in the published snapshot and in the page's inline `sp-data` JSON and calendar entries. A page whose auto-incidents fire often accumulates thousands of rows, and each visitor — or poll — pays for all of them, while `listIncidents` deliberately caps at `INCIDENT_LIST_LIMIT` (`StatusPagesService.ts:682`). ``` Bound the index the way the incident list is bounded: `.orderBy(["startedAt", "desc"]).limit(...)` with a named cap, and add a snapshot test for the cap. If the calendar must keep a full year of marks, aggregate the marked days in the query instead of carrying every incident title. ```
What was checked - `:esc` and script's `enc` produce identical bytes for `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028/9; footer hrefs go through `safeUrl("https:")` - `windowDays` padding matches script `shift`; `script.test.ts` and `render.test.ts` pin both copies to the same answers - `lastDays`/`timeBucket` index math keeps UTC day alignment (bars[64] = 2026-08-25, lone down day outside window)

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge Bounded-read edge case in the snapshot builder can hide an open incident, and the inline script's payload has no test pinning it. 1 warning −1 · 3 notes · tests partial −1 · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable Rebuilds the public status page in Maple's own layout: status banner, paged 90-day uptime history over a year, an incident calendar, and privacy/terms footer links end to end. Escaping, the SQL wiring and the nullable migration are sound; one bounded read can hide an incident that is still open. - `renderHero`, paged `windowDays` bars and a Monday-first calendar in `renderPage` - Snapshot carries 365 days of bars plus a bounded `incidentHistory` index - `privacy_url` / `terms_url` through DB, service validation, v2 API and editor - One inline script pages windows and months from an escaped JSON block ### Before merge - [ ] **Migration** · Check it is safe on production data and with the code still deployed · [`packages/db/drizzle/20261029152817_status_page_footer_links/migration.sql`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/8b79db50444ef79324977eb27f33ca4f7c03d43f/packages/db/drizzle/20261029152817_status_page_footer_links/migration.sql) - [ ] **Manual** · Existing pages only gain the year of history and the calendar on their next publish; snapshots published before decode with an empty `incidentHistory` and 90-day bars ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F3 · limit(500) after startedAt desc can drop an incident that is still open correctness · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts:373-377`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/8b79db50444ef79324977eb27f33ca4f7c03d43f/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts#L373-L377) The read is capped before `isListedIncident` runs, so the cap is applied to a set that includes incidents that are still open, however old they started. On a page with more than 500 published incidents in the year, an outage that started long ago and never resolved sorts last in `orderBy([startedAt, desc])` and is cut, so it disappears from `snapshot.incidents` (and `incidentHistory`) while it is still ongoing — the public page shows nothing happening. ``` Push the listed predicate into the query instead of filtering after the cap: `PG.or($.resolvedAt.isNull(), $.resolvedAt.gte(listedCutoff), $.scheduledStart.gte(startedAt))`, keeping the 500 cap only on the resolved tail. ```
🔵 Note · F4 · Incident index cutoff is a day wider than firstDay, so the oldest calendar day gains a false marker correctness · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts:288`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/8b79db50444ef79324977eb27f33ca4f7c03d43f/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts#L288) `indexCutoff` is the instant `nowMs - 365 days`, while the bars and the calendar start at `firstDay = utcDay(nowMs - 364 days)`, so incidents resolved in that one-day band are still indexed. `calendarDays` then clamps `first` up to `oldest` (`history.ts:189`) and the span collapses to one day, marking the oldest day of the calendar with an incident that resolved the day before it — visitors see "1 incident" on a day nothing happened. ``` const indexCutoff = Date.parse(`${firstDay}T00:00:00.000Z`) ```
🔵 Note · F5 · toContain("No data") passes on the bar tooltips, not the uptime span it covers tests · [`packages/status-page/src/render.test.ts:692`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/8b79db50444ef79324977eb27f33ca4f7c03d43f/packages/status-page/src/render.test.ts#L692) Every bar of `components[0]` has `checks === 0`, so all 90 render `title="…: No data"` (`format.ts:88`): the assertion holds even if `renderComponent` stops emitting `No data`, which is the branch this test was changed to cover. ``` expect(html).toContain('No data') ```
🔵 Note · F6 · PageData omits bars, len and end, so no test pins what the pager reads tests · [`packages/status-page/src/render.test.ts:197`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/8b79db50444ef79324977eb27f33ca4f7c03d43f/packages/status-page/src/render.test.ts#L197) `Schema.Struct` drops unknown keys on decode, so `pageDataOf` never sees the `bars`, `len` and `end` fields that `drawWindow` (`script.ts:27`) depends on. A regression in `pageData`'s bar mapping — for example emitting `[checks, downChecks]` or dropping the key — decodes cleanly and leaves every `pageDataOf` assertion green while paging renders empty bars. ``` Add `bar`-shaped fields to the `PageData` schema (`bars: Schema.Record(...)` of `Number | Tuple[Number, Number, Number]`, plus `len` and `end`) and assert one component's bar values. ```
What was checked - `scriptJson` escapes `<`, `>` and U+2028/9, and the script writes only via `textContent`/`setAttribute` - Footer links pass `safeUrl` (https only) and `escapeHtml` before reaching `href` - Migration adds two nullable text columns matching `packages/db/src/tables/status-pages.ts`

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge Held at 8 because a warning is open. 1 warning −1 · 3 notes · tests covered · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable This round moves the calendar index cutoff from "a year before now" to midnight UTC of the first bar day, matching the uptime bars, with a builder test that pins both sides of that boundary. The cutoff is correct; the year-wide cap on resolved incidents still has one gap. - `indexCutoff` starts at midnight UTC of `firstDay`, matching the bar window - New builder test pins the first bar day in and the day before out ### Before merge - [ ] **Migration** · Check it is safe on production data and with the code still deployed · [`packages/db/drizzle/20261029152817_status_page_footer_links/migration.sql`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/60144d42e0fc44122886abe9c439035a6ca09581/packages/db/drizzle/20261029152817_status_page_footer_links/migration.sql) ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F8 · limit(500) by startedAt desc drops a long-running incident the moment it resolves correctness · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts:382`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/60144d42e0fc44122886abe9c439035a6ca09581/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts#L382) The resolved read keeps only the 500 incidents with the newest `startedAt`, so an incident that started long ago and was just resolved is ordered last and never read. That is the incident seeded as "Long-running" in the test at `StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.test.ts:441`: set its `status` to `resolved` and it disappears from `snapshot.incidents` (where `isListedIncident` would list it for 14 days) and from `incidentHistory`, so a busy page silently drops the outage visitors were watching. inline.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Year-long incidents read has no `limit`, so the public page payload grows unbounded**
>
> <sub>F1 · Warning · performance</sub>

The cutoff moved from `STATUS_PAGE_INCIDENT_HISTORY_DAYS` (14) to `STATUS_PAGE_HISTORY_DAYS` (365) and the query still has no `limit` or `orderBy`, so every incident resolved in the last year (plus every unresolved one) is read and, through `incidentHistory`, embedded in the published snapshot and in the page's inline `sp-data` JSON and calendar entries. A page whose auto-incidents fire often accumulates thousands of rows, and each visitor — or poll — pays for all of them, while `listIncidents` deliberately caps at `INCIDENT_LIST_LIMIT` (`StatusPagesService.ts:682`).

```
Bound the index the way the incident list is bounded: `.orderBy(["startedAt", "desc"]).limit(...)` with a named cap, and add a snapshot test for the cap. If the calendar must keep a full year of marks, aggregate the marked days in the query instead of carrying every incident title.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Hero body claims no known issues under a non-operational banner**
>
> <sub>F2 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`renderHero` picks the body from `active.length` alone, while the headline and tint come from `overall`. With `auto_incidents: "off"` — or an incident not yet published — a failing monitor makes `overallStatus` `major_outage` with no active incident, so the page reads "We're experiencing a major outage" and directly under it "We're not aware of any issues affecting our systems."

```
Branch the body on `overall` too: show the all-clear only when `overall === "operational"`, otherwise say that live checks are failing and no incident has been posted, or name the components that are not operational.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`limit(500)` after `startedAt desc` can drop an incident that is still open**
>
> <sub>F3 · Warning · correctness</sub>

The read is capped before `isListedIncident` runs, so the cap is applied to a set that includes incidents that are still open, however old they started. On a page with more than 500 published incidents in the year, an outage that started long ago and never resolved sorts last in `orderBy([startedAt, desc])` and is cut, so it disappears from `snapshot.incidents` (and `incidentHistory`) while it is still ongoing — the public page shows nothing happening.

```
Push the listed predicate into the query instead of filtering after the cap: `PG.or($.resolvedAt.isNull(), $.resolvedAt.gte(listedCutoff), $.scheduledStart.gte(startedAt))`, keeping the 500 cap only on the resolved tail.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`limit(500)` by `startedAt desc` drops a long-running incident the moment it resolves**
>
> <sub>F8 · Warning · correctness</sub>

The resolved read keeps only the 500 incidents with the newest `startedAt`, so an incident that started long ago and was just resolved is ordered last and never read. That is the incident seeded as "Long-running" in the test at `StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.test.ts:441`: set its `status` to `resolved` and it disappears from `snapshot.incidents` (where `isListedIncident` would list it for 14 days) and from `incidentHistory`, so a busy page silently drops the outage visitors were watching. Read the recently-resolved detail set (for example `resolvedAt >= nowMs - STATUS_PAGE_INCIDENT_HISTORY_DAYS`) in its own uncapped query, like `open`, and keep the 500 cap only for the calendar index.

```
Add a second resolved read cut at `nowMs - STATUS_PAGE_INCIDENT_HISTORY_DAYS * DAY_MS` with no cap (merged with `open` into the detail set), and leave `limit(STATUS_PAGE_INCIDENT_INDEX_LIMIT)` to the year-wide calendar index only.
```
